Project standards v3 · stack node-ts · greenfield repository
These conventions are binding. Blocking rules and commands stop a release; a reviewer sees every other finding.
### Folder structure
- Required directories: src
- Allowed top-level entries: src, lib, app, pages, components, hooks, server, client, api, functions, test, tests, __tests__, e2e, packages, apps, bin, public, static, assets, styles, prisma, config, types, docs, scripts, .*, *.md, LICENSE*, LICENCE*, NOTICE*, CHANGELOG*, CODEOWNERS, Dockerfile*, Makefile, *.yml, *.yaml, *.lock, *.toml, *.json, *.js, *.cjs, *.mjs, *.ts, *.mts, *.html
- Files matching **/*.test.ts belong under: src, lib, app, pages, components, hooks, server, client, api, functions, test, tests, __tests__, e2e, packages, apps
- Files matching **/*.spec.ts belong under: src, lib, app, pages, components, hooks, server, client, api, functions, test, tests, __tests__, e2e, packages, apps
### Naming
- src/**/*.ts: kebab-case file names
- Test files sit beside or mirror the module they cover and end in .test.ts
### Comments
- Comment lines: at most 30% of added lines in any file with 20+ added lines
- Never leave commented-out code
- Never write these phrases in comments: "// rest of the code", "// rest of code", "// rest of the file", "// rest of the implementation", "// rest of the code goes here", "// rest of the code here", "// rest of the code remains", "// rest of the code unchanged", "// rest of the code remains unchanged", "// rest of the code remains the same", "// existing code here", "// existing code remains", "// existing code remains unchanged", "// existing code remains the same", "// implementation goes here", "// your implementation here", "// your code here", "// your code goes here", "// code goes here", "... rest of the code ...", "... existing code ...", "... remaining code ..."
### Testing
- Runner: npm test
- Test files: **/*.test.ts, **/*.spec.ts
- Every new module ships with a test file covering its failure paths
### Clean Code
Write clean, readable code:
- Use meaningful, intention-revealing names for variables, functions, and classes
- Functions should do one thing and do it well (under 20 lines where practical)
- Avoid magic numbers — use named constants
- No dead code, no commented-out code blocks left behind
- Prefer explicit early returns over deeply nested conditionals
### Self-Documenting Code
Write self-documenting code — minimize comments:
- Use descriptive variable and function names instead of inline comments
- Only add a comment when the WHY is non-obvious (a workaround, an invariant, a hidden constraint)
- Do not explain WHAT the code does — well-named identifiers already communicate that
- No multi-paragraph docstrings on trivial functions
### Test-Driven Development
Apply TDD practices:
- Write tests before or alongside implementation
- Each public function should have at least one unit test
- Tests must be independent, deterministic, and fast
- Cover edge cases: null/undefined inputs, empty collections, boundary values
- Mock external dependencies (databases, APIs, filesystem) in unit tests
### Robust Error Handling
Handle errors correctly at every layer:
- Never swallow exceptions silently — either handle them or propagate them
- Provide meaningful error messages with enough context to diagnose the problem
- Validate inputs at system boundaries (user input, external APIs)
- Use structured error types rather than generic Error strings where possible
- Log errors with stack traces and the relevant context at the time of failure

### SOLID Principles
Follow SOLID design principles:
- Single Responsibility: each class/function has one reason to change
- Open/Closed: open for extension, closed for modification
- Liskov Substitution: subtypes must be substitutable for their base types
- Interface Segregation: prefer small, focused interfaces over large monolithic ones

### Test-Driven Development
Apply TDD practices:
- Write tests before or alongside implementation
- Each public function should have at least one unit test
- Tests must be independent, deterministic, and fast
- Cover edge cases: null/undefined inputs, empty collections, boundary values
- Mock external dependencies (databases, APIs, filesystem) in unit tests
